In 1988, he was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and to the National Academy of Sciences in 1991, became Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in 1995, and won a Guggenheim Fellowship in 1996.[4][6][7] In 2012 he became a Fellow of the American Mathematical Society.[8] He received the 2014–15 Dean's Award for Lifetime Achievements in Teaching from Stanford University.[9] In 2015, he was elected vice president of the American Mathematical Society.[20] He was awarded an Honorary Doctor of Science from the University of Warwick in 2015.[21] He received the Wolf Prize in Mathematics for 2017, shared with Charles Fefferman.[22] In the same year, he was awarded the Heinz Hopf Prize, the Lobachevsky Medal and Prize by Kazan Federal University, and the Rolf Schock Prize.[23][24][25]
